name: Dash.

lifecycle.note: Pinned v6.3.4 has a bounded CPU/RAM shared recipe and no-account API adapter. RUNNING_IN_DOCKER=false avoids host namespace setup; disabling background collection prevents disabled storage/network/GPU collectors from running. CPU/RAM describe the visible Linux kernel, not the service cgroup quota. Full host observation and live acceptance remain separate.

security: The shared CPU/RAM profile grants no capabilities, namespace access or host mounts and uses a read-only root filesystem. The upstream full-host Compose grants privileged mode and host-root visibility; do not infer those grants from ordinary app approval.
Keep the unauthenticated dashboard on a private interface and review whether host inventory is appropriate for its viewers.
pitfalls: The shared profile intentionally provides only kernel-visible CPU/RAM. Native Linux Docker normally exposes kernel-wide /proc counters; Docker VM or virtualized /proc can expose another scope. CPU and memory limits bound Dashdot, not the reported counters. Independently compare scope before claiming physical-host metrics.

Widget selection alone is insufficient: pinned LazyObservable starts every collector when background collection is enabled. The recipe disables background collection and Docker-specific namespace setup explicitly.

The adapter validates configured scope and nonempty complete CPU/RAM data, not host identity, freshness, disks/network, Homarr widgets or restart persistence. Full host observation still needs separate source-bound authority and acceptance; no privilege bypass is published.
